title: Basketball Stats App
description: Basketball stats for leagues and teams, with live scoring and shot charts on the web and on phones.
details: The scorer taps a player and a play during the game, and the box score, shot chart and league standings update live for everyone following. Coaches get shot heatmaps by court zone and side-by-side player comparisons. The web app is React and the iOS and Android apps are React Native. They share TypeScript types in one Turborepo monorepo and talk to the same Convex backend.

title: UpSpeech
description: Software for speech therapy clinics that treat stuttering. Patients practice between sessions and the therapist follows every attempt.
details: UpSpeech helps speech-language pathologists treat stuttering. Patients follow a practice plan between sessions, and every attempt goes back to the therapist, who decides what happens next. I built the web platform end to end, including sessions, patient progress, multi-tenancy, auth and deployment. It's a Rails 8 API with a React and TypeScript frontend, shipped with Kamal. Now I'm building the React Native companion app for patients and clinicians.

title: MyAgentWebsite
description: Website builder for real estate agents. Each agent gets a branded site on their own domain, no developer needed.
details: Agents and small agencies sign up and get their own branded website on their own domain. One admin backoffice manages listings, blog posts, testimonials and newsletters for every site. A single Rails API serves three React frontends: the agent's public site, the admin dashboard and the marketing site. Everything runs on Railway and Vercel.

title: Therapy Resources
description: Therapists describe what they need for a session and get printable cards and games in their own illustration style.
details: Therapists and psychologists pick a visual style once, then generate session materials in it, such as emotion cards, flashcards, board games, posters and worksheets. Gemini draws the illustrations to match the style. A Konva canvas editor handles layout, and @react-pdf exports print-ready PDFs with an optional QR code. Therapists can publish what they make to a shared marketplace for others to reuse. The app runs in English and Portuguese, and it's a separate product from UpSpeech, built for a different market.

title: Basketball Video Analyzer
description: Free desktop app for basketball coaches to cut game film into tagged clips for the team.
details: I got tired of scrubbing through game tape in VLC, so I built this. Load a game, mark in and out points with keyboard shortcuts, and tag each clip with categories like pick and roll or transition. Category sets save as presets you can reuse across games. Coaches can draw on a clip, present clips full screen, or export them as folders for players. It runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, updates itself, and is open source.

title: Delivered Photos
description: Client galleries for photographers. Send one link, and the client hearts their picks on their phone.
details: A photographer uploads a shoot and sends the client one link. The client hearts the photos they want, sends the picks back, and downloads the finals. Two React and Vite apps, the photographer dashboard and the client gallery, share auth and schema on a Convex backend in a pnpm monorepo. Originals sit in S3 behind presigned URLs, and Dodo handles payments. It competes with Pixieset and ShootProof by being faster and simpler for photographers who deliver digitally.

title: FPB Calendar
description: Portuguese basketball fixtures and box scores, with any team's games synced to your calendar.
details: Calendário FPB scrapes the Portuguese Basketball Federation's site and builds a page for every competition, team, game and player. Players get a stat line going back several seasons. Pick a team and its games land in your calendar, through a Google Calendar invite or an ICS feed for Apple Calendar and Outlook. Background jobs keep fixtures and results current. Built with Sinatra and Sequel on Postgres, with Nokogiri doing the scraping.

title: CoinSprout
description: Money tracker for individuals and couples. Drop in a bank statement and it sorts every row for you.
details: Drop in a bank statement as a CSV, a PDF or a photo, and GPT-4o puts every transaction in a category. Couples can share accounts, split expenses and track who paid whom back. Budgets, savings goals, net worth and recurring transactions sit next to reports like a 90-day activity heatmap and month-over-month comparisons. The app leans on a garden theme, so goals are seeds you plant and your net worth grows from a first sprout into an oak. Built with Next.js and Convex.

title: KidShare
description: Co-parenting app for separated parents: shared expenses, the custody calendar and messages in one place.
details: KidShare gives two households one record of the kids' lives. A parent logs a cost and picks the split, and KidShare keeps a running statement of who owes whom, including recurring expenses and recorded payments. The custody calendar shows who has the kids each day and when the next handover is. Messages and family rules live next to the money. Built with React 19 on a Convex backend, installable as a PWA with push notifications, and deployed on Vercel.

title: ProTasca
description: Website builder for restaurants, with menus, reservations, online ordering and local SEO. It takes no commission on orders.
details: A restaurant signs up and gets a site filled in from its TheFork, Zomato and Google Business listings. Owners run everything from one backoffice, and ProTasca takes no cut of the orders. It reuses the MyAgentWebsite setup, a Rails API behind separate React apps for the public site, the backoffice and the marketing site.

title: Dois Agentes
description: An AI assistant for Portuguese real estate agents that keeps track of their deals and drafts the next step.
details: Dois Agentes is an assistant for real estate agents in Portugal. It is sold alongside MyAgentWebsite and can inherit its listings. Work reaches it when a message or a synced listing arrives, when a scheduled job runs, or when the agent asks it something. It keeps the agent's contacts, deals, visit sheets and valuations, and tracks each deal through a numbered service checklist. Agents can also consult specialists that cite the sources they used. It drafts, and the agent decides what goes out. Built as a single Rails 8 app with Hotwire and Solid Queue on Railway, with Claude models called through OpenRouter.

title: Cadence Studio
description: A one-person AI content studio where specialist agents draft in your voice and nothing publishes until you approve it.
details: Cadence runs a small team of specialist agents that write in your voice on a schedule you set. Drafts land in one review queue, next to a draft you already approved, so you can compare the voice side by side. Cadence checks every draft against 16 rules and a 27-word vocabulary watchlist. The queue marks what they catch, like em-dash asides and hedge openers. It switches between Claude, Gemini and OpenAI through the Vercel AI SDK, makes images with fal.ai, and publishes to Bluesky first. It is in private beta.

title: Analytics Hub
description: My own dashboard for every project I run. It pulls traffic, errors and deploys from ten sources and emails me once a week.
details: I built this to stop opening ten dashboards to check on my projects. Convex crons pull data from GA4, Search Console, Cloudflare, Vercel, Railway, GitHub, Sentry, Bing, Lighthouse and uptime checks. The Next.js home page lists the projects that need attention, and each project has its own pages for traffic, SEO, health, deploys and usage. Every Monday AhaSend sends me an HTML digest of the week.

title: Portfolio Site
description: This site. SvelteKit and Tailwind, with every project page built from one JSON file.
details: You're on it. Projects and experience live in JSON, and SvelteKit prerenders a page, an Open Graph image and structured data for each project at build time. The contact form posts to Formspree, so there's no backend to run. It has light and dark themes, and the motion switches off when your system asks for reduced motion.

title: IMKAUFMANN
description: Portfolio site and CMS for a photographer, with control over how each gallery is laid out.
details: I built this for a photographer starting out, so he could publish and manage his own work. He picks how each gallery displays, as a carousel, a grid or another layout, and uploads images to Cloudinary through CarrierWave. The CMS is custom, written in Rails with React components for previewing and editing.

title: Jovens Futuro
description: Blog platform where young adults write about what they care about. Every post gets SEO metadata and a social preview image.
details: Young writers publish posts through a WYSIWYG editor. Each article gets its own metadata, a readable URL and an Open Graph image that Cloudinary generates on the fly. Admins moderate posts from a Rails backend, and the front end uses React.

title: AOC Ruby (aoc_rb)
description: Ruby toolkit that sets up and runs Advent of Code puzzles. I contributed fixes and improvements.
details: aoc_rb fetches each day's Advent of Code input and sets up the files for you from the command line. I used it for my own runs, then sent back bug fixes and quality-of-life improvements.
